body.heading: About this sheet
paragraphs: Free SparkKindly Kids fold & make printable: Paper Aeroplane — Classic Dart.

The classic dart in six folds: crease the sheet lengthways, fold the top corners to the centre line, fold the slanted edges in once more, halve it, fold the wings down — and fly. Each step's diagram follows exactly from the one before, so small folders can check their paper against the picture at every stage.

body.heading: How to use it
paragraphs: Print the sheet, follow the numbered steps in order, and press every fold flat with the side of your hand. Check each fold reaches the centre line before pressing — a dart that matches the middle flies straight.

takeaway: Six careful folds turn one flat sheet into a flying machine — sequencing, symmetry and a first taste of aerodynamics in a single make.
materials: A printer and paper (plain copier paper flies best — no card stock)
A flat table for pressing creases
Crayons or markers to decorate the wings (optional)
supervision: Fold the first plane together, checking each step against the diagram, then let them fold the second solo and compare the two flights.
safetyNotes: Fly planes outside or in a big hall, and never aim at faces or animals — a folded paper nose is pointier than it looks.
Print at 100% size (not "fit to page") so the sheet keeps its true size and the pictures stay the size they were drawn.
screenFreeExtension: Run a flight contest outside: whose dart flies farthest? Fold a second plane, bend one wing tip up a little, and see what changes.
